newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $20 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $20 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $20 a tonne weaker on Monday, as prices are seen consolidating gains made on Friday, traders said.

An unexpectedly strong showing on the U.S. first quarter cocoa grind lifted prices on Friday, with July cocoa ending up $12 a tonne on the day at $1,463, having traded from $1,461 to $1,473. Spot May futures gained $19, to $1,437.

The grind figures rose by 20.74 percent compared with the same year-ago period, to 95,435 tonnes. The number was more than double most analysts' estimates and fueled an early speculative rally. Unable to challenge its overhead target, however, prices eased off the highs by the close.
Technically, July's next upside objective was seen at $1,480, while $1,433 was seen as key support level.
In London, cocoa futures fell early on sell stops and were lingering near the day's lows. May stood 17 stg a tonne lower at 1,002 stg per tonne, at the midday break.
